To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the stiff EOS describes well the experimental observables of the reaction systems, 2) multifragmentation with a cold fragment emission is predicted for all reactions, 3) semi-transparency is observed for reactions with 58 Ni and 92Mo, and 4) radial expansion and semi-transparency are the two main features of reactions at Fermi energy.
the reaction mechanisms in heavy ion collisions at Fermi energies depend on the reaction energy and mass asymmetry of the colliding systems.

the AntisymmetriZed Molecular Dynamics (AMD) model calculations with the stiff EOS give a consistent description of many direct experimental observables, including velocity spectra of light particles and IMF's, multiplicity distributions, and elliptic flow, and that the AMD model calculations with the soft equation of state predict a multifragmentation scenario in which cold fragments are formed and stay cold until multifragmentation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the dynamics of heavy ion reactions at Fermi energies.
the study of reaction mechanisms in the Fermi-energy region.
understanding the multifragmentation mechanism in heavy ion collisions at Fermi energies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reaction dynamics in Fermi energy reactions are sensitive to the EOS and the in-medium NN cross section.
the stiff EOS is favored by the data.
multifragmentation in these Fermi energy heavy-ion collisions is not due to the softness of the EOS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stiff EOS is more favored than the soft EOS in describing the reaction dynamics of the Fermi energy heavy-ion collisions studied here.
the stiff EOS with a density dependent effective nucleon-nucleus potential and an in-medium nucleon nucleon cross section is the preferred one for the Fermi energy heavy-ion reactions studied.
the stiff EOS and the Antisymmetized Molecular Dynamics model can be used to study the dynamics and multifragmentations at Fermi energy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stiff EOS, which is consistent with the nuclear matter saturation density, gives a better description of the experimental data than the soft EOS.

the reaction dynamics and fragment production in the Fermi-energy heavy-ion collisions are sensitive to the stiffness of the EOS and the strength of the NN cross section, but insensitive to the details of the in-medium NN cross section.
the multifragmentation process is a common feature for all reactions studied in this work.
